Class RouteLocator

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.web.router.RouteLocator
@Internal public final class RouteLocator extends Object
The target of a locator route, see HttpRouteScope.locate(String, LocatorHandler, Function). The route matches its prefix followed by the rest of the path, for every standard HTTP method. When the router selects it, the router runs the locator and matches the rest of the path with the routes of the RouteTable of the LocatedRoutes of the located target, and answers the route of that table, with the path variables of both and the target, instead of the locator route. The table may have locator routes too, which locate again. The table of a LocatedRoutes is built by the RouteTableFactory of the routes, on the first target it routes.
Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • uriTemplate

      public static String uriTemplate(UriRouteMatch<?,?> match)
      The URI template of the routes of a match, including the prefixes of the locator routes that located a route of a located target, e.g. /shops/{shop}/items/{item} for the located route /items/{item} under the prefix /shops/{shop}: the template of the request, e.g. for the metrics and the traces, see BasicHttpAttributes.getUriTemplate(HttpRequest).
      Parameters:
      match - A match
      Returns:
      The URI template of its route, under the prefixes of the locator routes for a located route

    • whenLocated

      public static @Nullable CompletionStage<?> whenLocated(HttpRequest<?> request)
      Completes when the asynchronous locators that have not located their targets for the request yet have, e.g. for a filter that needs the routes of the request before they are matched: the routes of a located target are known once its locator located it. Finding the routes again may start the locators of the located routes, which may be pending again.
      Parameters:
      request - The request
      Returns:
      A stage that completes with a non-null value when the pending locators completed, or null if none is pending
      Since:
      5.3.0

    • abandonPendingLocations

      public static void abandonPendingLocations(HttpRequest<?> request)
      Stop waiting for the asynchronous locators that have not located their targets for the request yet, e.g. when the client went away: matching the request fails instead of waiting for a target no one receives a response for, and the stages of the locators no longer reference the request. The stages are not cancelled: a locator may return a stage it shares with other requests, e.g. of a cache, which they keep waiting for.
      Parameters:
      request - The request
      Since:
      5.3.0
